question.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1} \\ -3{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-7{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2}=-9 \\ -3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=3 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the first and the second equations we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} & =-6 \\ {x}_{2} & =3,\end{aligned}
$$

which we substitute into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=3 \\ -3{x}_{1}+5(3) & =3 \\ -3{x}_{1} & =-12 \\ {x}_{1} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2}=3$ into the third equation and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ (4)-(3) & =1 \\ 1 & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2}=3,$ which means

$$
4{a}_{1}+3{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=4+3=7.
$$
